issues: s148-band1 row3: the XML has 'יוֹדְעֵי דָת וְדִין' (shva under the vav). The print appears to have qamats: 'וָדִין'. Fix only if an enlarged image confirms it.

The print appears to read 'נָקִי', with qamats under nun and hiriq under qof, the same form as 'אִי נָקִי' later on that row. This is a vowel difference, not a request to normalize to Daniel 7:9.
s151-band2 row5: the XML has 'יִגְזוֹר וְיִפְתְּחוּ'. The print appears to read 'וְיִפָּתְחוּ', with a qamats under pe.

s146-band2 row5, last word: the XML has 'לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּתֹהוּ' (shva under kaf). The print appears to have a horizontal stroke (patach) under kaf: 'כַּתֹהוּ'. I can't tell from the band whether tav has a dagesh. Please check only the kaf vowel and do not take the reading from MT.

None of these sites affects human answers 269–275, which are closed.
verified: The earlier finding that one לְמַעְלָה should be deleted was wrong. melekh-two-lemaalah.png and s150-band3 row4 both clearly print 'וְעַד לְמַעְלָה לְמַעְלָה רַבּוֹת'. The XML keeps both words, which is correct.

The human readings are encoded exactly at their sites. 269: 'אוּלַי יֵחָנֵן' (s148-band1 row3). 270: 'אַרְקָא. בְּבוּקָה' and 271: 'הִסְתַּכֵּל בְּתַבְנִית' (s150-band1 row7). 272: 'בְּכִנּוּי מְחֻזָּקָה' (s150-band2 row3). 273: 'מְעֻזָּקָה' and 274: 'שָׁכֵן בְּחָזְקָה' (s150-band2 row4). 275: 'שְׁרֵא נְהוֹרָא' (s151-band1 row4). I did not reopen them, and the print does not contradict them.

All 25 primary corrections are in the XML and match the bands. They are: רֶנֶן בְּעֶרֶץ, עֶרֶץ, חוֹרֵי, יִפְעַל, לְהִזָּכֵר, לְבִצָּרוֹן, בַּשּׁוֹפָר וְקוֹרְאֵי, בְּמִשְׁפָּט on s148, זָרַע, לַתָּם, וּבְחַפֶּשְׂךָ, הִזָּכֵר, יָצְאָה, וְנַפְשׁוֹת, וּבַעֲטָרָה, וּבִדְמוּת, וְנֹגַהּ, בְּמִשְׁפָּט on s150, כְּנוֹפֶת, לֶהָבוֹת, כְּקֶרַח, בְּיָמִין, בְּכֵן, לְהִתְעַנּוֹת and וָנֵזֶר.
The earlier human readings 'וְכַעֲלוֹת שׁוֹפַר מִדַּלֵּי' (s148) and 'וְיֻקְדַּשׁ בְּאַחַת מִשָּׁלֹשׁ' (s151) are unchanged.

The 'סלוק.' description is printed above the first line on s146 and is encoded as type=description before the poem text. The ק׳ speaker label is placed outside the second Ps 8:10b seg and its milestones.

The half-verse sources match the existing WLC ranges in existing-wlc-halfverse-proof.json. Each printed quotation ends where the WLC range ends: Prov 29:4a 'מֶלֶךְ בְּמִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִיד אָרֶץ.', Ps 8:10b twice, Ps 97:1a 'יְיָ מָלָךְ תָּגֵל הָאָרֶץ.' and Ps 96:1b 'שִׁירוּ לַיְיָ כָּל הָאָרֶץ:'. Isa 6:3b keeps its WLC words but in a different order, so it is correctly typed adaptation. No new verse boundaries were invented, and no hypothetical ole exception was applied.

Every chapter, verse and half-verse milestone has its own bare terminator of the same unit. Each occurrence uses its own corresp (psalms_8_first and psalms_8_second), so no corresp is repeated. The earth, judgment, merit and mystical prayer-part milestones are in order, and a final terminator closes them.

English: earth, judgment, merit and all six quotation corresp sets are shared one to one with the Hebrew. The mystical part is Hebrew-only, so under the alignment rule it is set inside the merit row with no English beside it. No English was supplied for the mystical sections. The English body text is identical to the accepted payload listed in english-preservation-proof.json.

The head 'סֵדֶר אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ.' and all 38 petitions on s156 and s158 match the bands in consonants, visible vowels, maqaf and the final ':'. The damaged aleph on s158 row4 is a print defect only.

The '*)' marker is printed at the mena petition, and the German note targets avinu_malkenu/mena. Its text, the order of the abbreviated petitions and the rafe on פֿ match the last five lines of s156-band3.

The final abbreviation glyph cannot be read at band resolution. The XML encodes it as א״<c cert="low">ז</c>״וו, which marks honestly that the source is unclear. It is not a silent conjecture. The human answer to 276 says 'not sure', and the XML keeps it tentative and does not upgrade it. The English note (resp codex) calls 'und so weiter' an editorial interpretation, not a source reading.

Both custom routes give all 38 petitions exactly once. The uncertain abbreviation is never used to leave any petition out. The printed phrase 'in Fürth and some congregations' is kept in the rubric 'כמנהג פירטה וכמה קהלות', so the existing fuerth feature is enough.

Both are encoded with English text: s156 as a witness to the Hebrew page, s157 as the English counterpart. The English for all 38 petitions on s157 and s159 matches the encoded words, and every petition corresp is shared with the Hebrew.
